== CUSTOM OBJECT XML FORMAT == File path: objects/ObjectName__c.object metadataType: CustomObject memberName: ObjectName__c <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <CustomObject xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <label>Object Label</label> <pluralLabel>Object Labels</pluralLabel> <description>Optional description</description> <nameField> <label>Name Field Label</label> <type>Text</type> <!-- Text or AutoNumber --> <!-- if AutoNumber: <displayFormat>RES-{0000}</displayFormat> --> </nameField> <deploymentStatus>Deployed</deploymentStatus> <sharingModel>ReadWrite</sharingModel> <!-- NEW objects with no MasterDetail: ReadWrite. Objects with MasterDetail: MUST be ControlledByParent --> <enableBulkApi>true</enableBulkApi> <enableStreamingApi>true</enableStreamingApi> <enableReports>false</enableReports> <!-- set true only if ticket explicitly requires reports --> <enableActivities>false</enableActivities> <!-- set true only if ticket explicitly requires activities --> <enableHistory>false</enableHistory> <!-- set true only if ticket explicitly requires field history --> </CustomObject> RULE - RECORD IDENTIFIER FIELDS (applies to Text AND AutoNumber, for ANY object — evaluate this fresh every time using the object actually being created, never limited to names seen in examples): Every custom object requires a <nameField>. Before creating any field from the ticket's field list, check its API name against the pattern <ObjectName>_Name__c or <ObjectName>_Number__c, where <ObjectName> is literally the SAME name as the object currently being created — substitute the real object name each time, this is a structural pattern, not a fixed list of field names to match against. Example of applying the pattern generically: object Widget__c + a listed field Widget_Name__c or Widget_Number__c → that field matches. A field matching this pattern for the CURRENT object is that object's identifier field, not a separate custom field: - Configure <nameField> directly with that field's type (Text stays Text, AutoNumber stays AutoNumber), label, and any format details (length for Text; displayFormat/startingNumber for AutoNumber). - Do NOT also emit it as a separate custom field. Doing so creates two fields with the same label and purpose — a duplicate, not two distinct pieces of data. - Every OTHER field in the ticket's list (lookups, picklists, email, unrelated Text/Number fields, etc.) is unaffected by this rule and must still be created normally as its own field. - Only create a genuinely separate custom field alongside the nameField when the ticket clearly wants two distinct values that do NOT match this object-name-based pattern.
RULE: When creating an object, you MUST also generate: - A CustomTab file (see Tab format below) - A Profile file for Admin tab visibility (see Profile format below)
== CUSTOM TAB XML FORMAT == File path: tabs/ObjectName__c.tab metadataType: CustomTab memberName: ObjectName__c <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <CustomTab xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <customObject>true</customObject> <motif>Custom18: Form</motif> </CustomTab>
== PROFILE TAB VISIBILITY + FIELD PERMISSIONS XML FORMAT == File path: profiles/Admin.profile metadataType: Profile memberName: Admin <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <Profile xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <fieldPermissions> <editable>true</editable> <field>ObjectName__c.FieldName__c</field> <readable>true</readable> </fieldPermissions> <!-- repeat <fieldPermissions> for EVERY custom field on the object --> <tabVisibilities> <tab>ObjectName__c</tab> <visibility>DefaultOn</visibility> </tabVisibilities> </Profile> FIELD PERMISSIONS RULES: 1. Include one <fieldPermissions> block per custom field being created. 2. If the ticket specifies which profiles should have access, generate a separate Profile file for EACH mentioned profile with the appropriate fieldPermissions. 3. If no profiles are mentioned, generate fieldPermissions for the Admin profile only — the system will automatically grant access to the triggering user's profile as well. 4. editable=true + readable=true → field is visible and editable (use for normal fields). 5. editable=false + readable=true → field is visible but read-only (use for Formula, Roll-Up Summary, AutoNumber fields). 6. Do NOT include fieldPermissions for Required fields — Salesforce grants implicit access to those. 7. Do NOT include fieldPermissions for the object's Name field, including when a ticket-listed field (Text or AutoNumber — see the RECORD IDENTIFIER FIELDS rule above) was folded into <nameField> instead of being created as its own field. The Name field is never a separate CustomField component, for ANY object — referencing ObjectName__c.ObjectName_Name__c or ObjectName__c.ObjectName_Number__c (substitute whatever object/field you actually folded) in fieldPermissions fails deploy with "no CustomField named X found" because there is no such component to attach the permission to. This applies every time RECORD IDENTIFIER FIELDS applies, regardless of the object's name.
